input.content:
Six weeks after Skycast 1.0 shipped, the data taught us more than the roadmap ever did.

We're a team of three who built one Android and iOS app for a 7-day forecast. Two weeks before launch we handed a beta to 40 users. They found 11 bugs; we fixed 9 before 1.0. Three lessons stuck:

1. Real users beat guesses. Crash rate dropped from 4% of sessions in the beta to 0.5% after launch, mostly by removing a background refresh that ran on low memory.

2. Cache before you optimize. App start went from 3.2 seconds to 1.1 seconds once we cached the last forecast on the device instead of waiting for the network.

3. Cut what nobody opens. Hourly radar maps took a third of design time in month one, and only 2 of 40 beta users opened them. We shipped without them.

Six weeks in: 4.6 from 310 ratings. Top complaint: no widget yet.

What's one feature you cut before launch and never missed?
